ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver, on trip TRP-02804. The route deviation is established and part of the fare is returned.

THE DEVIATION. On the governing trace figure (EV-GPS-02804, trace_distance_km 29.13 km), the trip ran 29.13 km against a booked optimal of 22.1 km (EV-TRIP-02804), an excess of 7.03 km, or 31.81%. POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern over the rounded trip-record copy of 29.1 km. Both establishment tests pass - the excess is more than 20% of optimal and more than 0.8 km - so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. The trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-02804 with consistent timestamps, so the rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged and the burden shifts to the driver.

THE DRIVER'S EXPLANATION. The driver's statement that traffic was heavy and that he took another road names no road, segment or advisory. POL-RD-03 requires a traffic_advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses, with an overlapping validity window and a matching diversion, and POL-RD-13 requires a traffic assertion to be tested against the advisory for this trip and nothing else. No advisory covers this trip window: EV-ADVIS-02804-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and the assertion carries no weight. Because the driver cited no advisory identifier, POL-RD-13(1) applies - this is a gap in the bundle, not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact - so POL-RD-10(5) is not triggered. The deviation stands at the measured figure.

NO OTHER EXONERATION. The chat log is empty (EV-CHAT-02804, 0 messages), so there is no rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04 and no waypoint to test. The trip record shows no amendment of the pickup or dropoff (original_pickup, original_dropoff, pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at all null, amended_optimal_distance_km null), so POL-RD-05 cannot be run. vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not displace the booked optimal of 22.1 km.

THE REMEDY. The fare is METERED (EV-FARE-02804), so POL-RD-02 governs and POL-RD-11 does not apply. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 22.1 + 0.28 x 29.8) x 1.2 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.50 on-optimal-route ERP = 36.7628. The 1.2 surge multiplier is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, the only artifact that carries it. Refund = charged_total 45.82 - 36.7628 = 9.0572, rounded up to SGD 9.10. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and well below the 90% full-refund share (19.77% of charged_total), so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of 9.10.

ERP. The single ERP line (PIE Eunos westbound, 1.50) is a genuine crossing on the optimal corridor - the nearest trace fix is 35.32 m away, inside the 250 m match radius - and it is already included in the recomputed fare. Under POL-RD-09(1) it is itemised for transparency only and is not added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure. Off-optimal-route ERP is 0.00, so no separate pass-through correction is due, and there is no billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4): no unmatched charge line and no airport surcharge.

REPEAT-DEVIATION CHECK. POL-RD-06 requires the driver profile to be consulted where the deviation is MATERIAL. I record that this deviation is established but not material: 7.03 km does not exceed the 8.0 km gate and 31.81% does not exceed the 50% gate. The mandatory consult is therefore not triggered, and the driver advocate's description of the deviation as material is incorrect on the figures, though nothing turns on it. In any event the citable fields show no pattern - deviation_flags_90d is 1, below 3, and 1 / 329 completed_trips_90d is 0.003, below 0.05 - so there is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral.

PROFILE FIELDS. On the rider's profile, deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 extra-corroboration requirement for a serial claimant is not triggered. The other profile fields mentioned by both sides (ratings, lifetime counters, prior_*) are context only under POL-GEN-01 and ground nothing. The rider's claim that the trip record and the fare breakdown independently corroborate the excess is not accepted as independence - both derive from the same trace measurement - but nothing turns on it, because independent corroboration is required only where the trace is impaired (it is not) or where a clause demands a second source (none does here).

DRIVER COMPENSATION. None is due. The POL-RD-04 compensation limb requires the billed distance to fall more than 1.0 km short of the trace; here the ledger bills 29.1 km against a 29.13 km trace, a shortfall of 0.03 km.

THE AMOUNT. The rider contests 8.50 and the rider's advocate argues the refund should be capped there. I do not cap it. POL-RD-02 defines the refund arithmetically from charged_total and the recomputed fare and states no cap, and this policy names every cap it intends (ERP 12.00, compensation 15.00, escalation ceiling 150.00). The money block's payable figure for this trip is 9.10, which is the arithmetic result.

NO ESCALATION. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c): 229 fixes at a 10-second interval over 100% coverage, zero gaps, maximum gap 0 seconds, no jump over 500 m, so no independent corroboration was needed. Trip identifiers and timestamps agree; no exculpatory clause was invoked against a cited missing artifact; the refund is far below both the 150.00 ceiling and charged_total; and no charge line lacks a counterpart in the trace or trip record. Confidence is 0.90, the decision resting on artifacts of full weight (EV-GPS-02804, EV-TRIP-02804, EV-FARE-02804).

EXECUTION. The monetary effect of 9.10 exceeds the 8.00 execution threshold, so this ruling is issued but held for human release under POL-GEN-05. It is a provisional ruling and either party may appeal it once under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
